title: The Geometry of Contextual Relations: Language Models Address Facts by Order of Mention
abstract: arXiv:2610.00910v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Human reasoning depends on how objects are related within propositions. \textit{How do relations organize the language representations of contextual contents?} We give an LLM a list of facts in its context (e.g., \emph{Alice eats an apple. Bob eats a pear.}) and measure how its hidden state changes when the question switches from what Alice eats to what Bob eats. Averaged over many lists, this change is a steering vector, which we call the \emph{ordinal vector}. It points to a fact by its \emph{order of mention}, the order in which the facts were stated in the context. We find that LLMs represent the fact a question asks about by its order of mention, not by the name the question contains. translated_title: 语境关系的几何结构：语言模型按提及顺序对事实进行寻址
translated_abstract: 人类推理依赖于命题中对象之间的关联方式。那么，关系如何组织语境内容的语言表示？我们在语言模型的上下文中给出一系列事实（例如：Alice吃一个苹果。Bob吃一个梨。），并测量当问题从“Alice吃什么”切换到“Bob吃什么”时，模型隐藏状态如何变化。在大量列表上取平均后，这一变化构成一个引导向量，我们称之为“序数向量”。该向量按事实被提及的顺序——即事实在上下文中被陈述的顺序——指向对应事实。我们发现，语言模型是通过提及顺序来表示问题所询问的事实，而不是通过问题中包含的名字。我们将这一现象表述为“序数寻址假设”：每种提及顺序在模型状态中都对应一个“事实地址”，该地址在所有上下文之间共享；问题会将状态移动到其询问事实对应的事实地址，而上下文……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 语言模型通过事实在上下文中的提及顺序而非问题中的实体名称来寻址所询问的事实，存在一个跨上下文共享的“序数向量”将隐藏状态引导至对应的事实地址。
en_tdlr: Language models address the fact a question asks about by its order of mention rather than by the entity name, with a shared "ordinal vector" steering the hidden state to a context-independent fact address.
